question: Does OpenAdapt's API tier (PR #1269, the 3.33 s vs 22.45 s figure in PR #1365) run on the OpenEMR referral under the current gates?
answer: No. On current main the compiler refuses to propose an API step for this form, so a gated run of the referral uses the GUI path and the API-tier speed-up does not apply.
how: Offline recompile, no app and no model: openemr_local_demo.compile_recording on the recording the #1374 measurement used, then propose_api_step(replace=True), as benchmark/openemr_api_tier/feature_e2e.py cmd_compile does.

recording.location: outside the repository (holds a synthetic patient's values and a network capture)

reasons: the form validates with rules the API step can't evaluate (form_DOB pastDate); it stays on the GUI
the form validates with rules the API step can't evaluate (form_DOB pastDate); it stays on the GUI

which_change_refuses_it: #1371 (enforce native form validation; leave script validation to the GUI). The session notes record that #1370 (refuse an API step whose span also wrote) also refuses it, because OpenEMR posts execute_background_services.php while the form is filled; the compiler reports the first reason only.

earlier_figures_and_their_gates.gates: plain replayer; API step admitted by the harness; no approval, no durable run, no run gate

earlier_figures_and_their_gates.figure: median engine 1.12 s (API) vs 15.95 s (GUI), 20 runs each
earlier_figures_and_their_gates.gates: each_item approval + durable run; no run gate; engine 352af585b, before #1367-#1372

consequence_for_the_lifecycle_comparison: The openadapt_api arm runs the same certified GUI program as the openadapt arm; its describe() records the refusal. Per-item cost and time for OpenAdapt on this workflow are the GUI path's.
